title: Backups
intro: Backups are made by the siem-backup service on the server. Every backup is encrypted with the backup password, known only to the server administrator – the panel does not store it. Passwords and keys for the destination are encrypted by the panel with the backup service key; once saved they cannot be read, only replaced.

secret.stale: saved with an old service key – enter it again

requested: requested – the backup service performs it within a few seconds
saved: Saved – the backup service applies the settings within a minute.

offline.title: The backup service is not responding
offline.lastSeen: Last contact: {{date}}. Scheduled backups are not being made.
offline.never: The siem-backup service has not reported yet (the backup container on the server).

noPass.title: No backup password
text: Without a password no backups are made. The server administrator sets it once with
in the stack directory and stores it off the server (the installer does this automatically).

passIdTip: A hash of the password that encrypts the backups – not the password itself. The same identifier is in the name of every backup, so you can see which password opens it. Only the server administrator knows the password (./backup.sh password show).
testTip: write and read at the destination

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.hint: Server time. A backup whose time passed while the server was off runs after it starts.

include.title: Content
include.sagaHint: accounts and roles, agents and their certificates, groups, alerts, panel rules, the NIS2 archive catalog, policies, notification channels
include.configHint: certificates (with the agents CA key) and the .env file with service passwords
include.archiveHint: new segments and manifests since the previous backup – sent only to the destination (the archive is already on the server disk)
include.grafanaHint: dashboards and settings changed in the Grafana UI (dashboards from the repository are restored without a backup)
include.warning: Without the Saga database and the server configuration the system cannot be restored after losing the server: agents would not trust the new server, and accounts and settings would have to be recreated.
include.events: Events in ClickHouse are not backed up – after restoring a server the last days are replayed from the NIS2 archive (Urd → Replay).

retention.title: Retention
retention.hint: A backup is removed when it is older than the given number of days or when there are more backups than the limit. The newest backup is always kept. NIS2 archive batches at the destination expire only by days.

target.title: Destination
target.localOnly: Backups stay only on this server's disk – a failure of the server or its disk takes them along with the system.

pathHint.sftp: starting with / – an absolute path, otherwise relative to the user's home directory
pathHint.smb: directory in the share (empty – the share root)
pathHint.s3: prefix in the bucket (empty – the root)

target.authServerKey: SSH key generated by the backup service (recommended – the private key never leaves the server)
addKey: of the user on the backup server (in TrueNAS: user account → SSH public key):
target.noKey: The backup service has no SSH key yet – generate one.
target.newKeyConfirm: The new key replaces the current one – the old one stops working. Continue?
target.privateKeyHint: OpenSSH or PEM format, without a passphrase
hostKey: – if it changes, uploads stop (protection against impersonation).

confirm.title: Save backup settings
confirm.text: Backup settings decide where the data of the whole system goes – confirm the change with your password.

restore.how1: You choose a backup and the parts to restore; first inspect its content (decryption with the backup password).
restore.how2: The backup service backs up the current state (you can go back to it) and fetches the chosen backup from the destination.
restore.how3: Within a minute the server stops the services using the database, restores the chosen parts and starts the stack – the panel is briefly unavailable, and after a database restore you have to sign in again.
restore.how4: The NIS2 archive is restored on a clean server with restore.sh (docs/en/operations.md).
restore.preparing: The backup service is preparing the restore…
restore.refreshHint: The list refreshes itself every 15 minutes and after every backup.
restore.title: Restore from the backup of {{when}}
restore.bothHint: restored together – .env holds the database role passwords; accounts, agents, certificates, alerts, policies, backup settings, certs/ and .env
restore.safety: Back up the current state first (recommended)
restore.safetyHint: lets you go back to the state before the restore
restore.warn1: The database returns to its state from {{when}}: alerts, settings changes, accounts and agents registered later will disappear.
restore.warn2: Agents registered after this date must enrol again.
restore.warn3: The panel will be briefly unavailable; after the restore sign in again (with the password valid on the backup date).
restore.warn4: Events in ClickHouse and the NIS2 archive are not changed.
restore.requested: Restore requested – the backup service prepares the backup and the server restores it within a few minutes.
